question: What are the required documents for the pre-assessment of a new business permit in Davao City?
reference_answer:
For NEW business permit pre-assessment, the charter lists the following requirements. Apply the ownership, representation, vehicle and activity conditions stated in each row. Source: Business Bureau printed pages 41-42 (PDF pages 2-3). These transcribed rows include their Where to Secure entries.

1. Duly filled-out Unified Application Form (1 original) Business Bureau or at the Web site https://busbureau.davaocity.gov.ph/ or apply online at https://appbts.davaocity.gov.ph/
2. Sketch / Google map of Business location (1 original) with pictures of the premise location Applicant
3. Certified List of Employees / Certification of no Employee (1 original) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
4. Valid DTI Registration for Single Proprietorship (1 photocopy) Department of Trade and Industry
5. SEC Registration, Articles of Incorporation for Partnership and Corporation (1 photocopy) Securities and Exchange Commission
6. Certificate of Cooperation, Articles of Cooperation for Cooperative (1 photocopy). Cooperative Development Authority
7. DOLE / POEA Certificate of Registration, if applicable. Department of Labor and Employment
8. DHSUD Certificate of Registration, if applicable. Department of Human Settlement and Urban Development
9. Special Power of Attorney (1 current and original) for represented – Sole Proprietorship Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
10. Partnership Resolution (1 current and original) for represented – Partnership Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
11. Secretary’s Certificate or Board Resolution for other form of ownership (1 current and original) - Corporation and Cooperative Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
12. Valid I.D. of representatives, owners (Sole Proprietor, OPC, Partnership), and Corporate Secretary (Corporation, Cooperative) - 1 photocopy each) Applicant
13. Contract of Lease and copy of the Proof of ownership by the Lessor if business location is not owned and is rented by the applicant (1 photocopy) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
14. Any proof of ownership if Business location is owned Applicant
15. consent and copy of any proof of ownership if business location is not owned and is freely used by the applicant (1 photocopy) Applicant
16. OR/CR of vehicle, if with delivery vehicle (1 photocopy each vehicle) Applicant
17. Consent for use of the vehicle if not owned by the applicant. Applicant
18. FSIC for Occupancy Permit valid in the last 9 months Bureau of Fire Protection
19. Affidavit of Undertaking that there had been no substantial changes made on the building Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
20. Other Requirements depending on the Business Activity declared Concerned Agency

question: What are the requirements and service fees to change my registered business address at the Business Bureau?
reference_answer:
For Amendment of Business Permit - Change of Business Address, the charter lists the following requirements (printed pages 42-43; PDF pages 3-4). Preserve the stated business-form and representation conditions. Each row below includes its Where to Secure entry.

1. Current Original Mayor’s Permit, Application for Renewal of Business Permit, or Certified True Copy of Business Permit w/ Affidavit of Loss in case of lost permits Applicant or Records Section, Business Bureau or Any Notary Public for affidavit of loss.
2. Application Affidavit of Change of Business Address (notarized) stating the new location of the business-Single Proprietorship Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
3. For Sole Proprietorship, if represented, Special Power of Attorney, indicating specific authority and capacity granted to representative. Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
4. For Partnership, Partnership Resolution indicating specific authority and capacity granted to representative, and stating the new location of the business Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
5. For Corporation / Cooperative, Board Resolution or Secretary’s Certificate, indicating specific authority and capacity granted to representative, and stating the new location of the business Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
6. Valid ID of the representative (1 photocopy), if newly designated Applicant
7. Sketch / Google map of Business location (1 original) with pictures of the premise location Applicant
8. Tax Declaration of the Property or any proof of property ownership (owned, rented and not rented) and Lease Contract if rented or Consent from Property Owner if not rented Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
9. FSIC for Occupancy Permit valid in the last 9 months Bureau of Fire Protection
10. Affidavit of Undertaking that there had been no substantial changes made on the building Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public

Fees (printed page 78; PDF page 39): Step 1 application lists None. For Step 2 payment at the City Treasurer’s Office, the charter states: Mayor’s Permit Fee is based on the asset size and nature of business. Service fee is Php50.00. The PHP 50.00 service fee is not a quoted total inclusive of the variable Mayor’s Permit Fee.

question: When does a Davao City business permit expire and what are the basic requirements to renew it in January?
reference_answer:
Business permit validity and renewal (printed page 54; PDF page 15): The Business Permit is granted for a period of not more than one (1) year and shall expire on the thirty-first (31st) of December following the date of issuance unless revoked or surrendered earlier. The Business Permit issued shall be renewed within the month of January. It shall have a continuing validity only upon renewal thereof and payment of the corresponding fee.

The RENEWAL checklist (printed pages 55-56; PDF pages 16-17) lists the following seven rows. Each transcribed row includes its Where to Secure entry; preserve the conditions and document quantities as stated.

3. For Partnership, Partnership Resolution, indicating specific authority and capacity granted to representative. Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
4. For other form of ownership, Board Resolution or Secretary’s Certificate, indicating specific authority and capacity granted to representative. Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
5. Valid I.D. of the representative (1 photocopy), if newly designated Applicant
6. Valid Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (1 photocopy) Applicant or Bureau of Fire Protection
7. Specific requirements for specific line of business Concerned Agency

However, for the renewal of a business permit, one of the requirements is a Tax Clearance. According to [S2], the Tax Clearance can be obtained at Counter 8, Tax Clearance Section, Real Property Tax Division (CTO Poblacion), or through assigned personnel at the CTO District Offices. The Tax Clearance is issued after 20 minutes of processing [S2]. The Tax Clearance is based on the 2017 Revenue Code of the City of Davao Ordinance No. 0291-17, series of 2017, section 7 [S2]. For more detailed information about the business permit renewal process and its expiration, it is recommended to check the Citizens' Charter of the Business Permit and Licensing Office in Davao City. [Wala akoy nakit-an nga impormasyon bahin niini sa Citizens' Charter.]

question: Kanus-a ga-expire ang business permit sa Davao ug unsa ang mga requirements para mag-renew karong Enero?
reference_answer:
Business permit validity and renewal (printed page 54; PDF page 15): The Business Permit is granted for a period of not more than one (1) year and shall expire on the thirty-first (31st) of December following the date of issuance unless revoked or surrendered earlier. The Business Permit issued shall be renewed within the month of January. It shall have a continuing validity only upon renewal thereof and payment of the corresponding fee.

The RENEWAL checklist (printed pages 55-56; PDF pages 16-17) lists the following seven rows. Each transcribed row includes its Where to Secure entry; preserve the conditions and document quantities as stated.

1. List of Employees stating the Name and Position of the Employees (1 copy) Applicant
2. For Sole Proprietorship, if represented, Special Power of Attorney, indicating specific authority and capacity granted to representative. Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
3. For Partnership, Partnership Resolution, indicating specific authority and capacity granted to representative. Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
4. For other form of ownership, Board Resolution or Secretary’s Certificate, indicating specific authority and capacity granted to representative. Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
5. Valid I.D. of the representative (1 photocopy), if newly designated Applicant
6. Valid Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (1 photocopy) Applicant or Bureau of Fire Protection
7. Specific requirements for specific line of business Concerned Agency

question: Who is required to secure an Occupational Permit, how much is the fee, and what is the penalty for late renewal?
reference_answer:
According to the Occupational Permit section of the thesis source charter (printed pages 104-106; PDF pages 65-67):

The charter states that an Occupational Permit is issued to any worker or employee who is not a holder of validly issued Professional Tax Receipts, whether working on a temporary or permanent basis.

Under Who may avail, it lists Filipino employees or workers aged 18 at application; foreigners may apply after securing an Alien Employment Permit from DOLE. Where the law allows a person below 18 to work, an Affidavit of Consent from the parent or guardian is required.

Renew annually on or before January 31. The charter states a 25% penalty for late renewal.

The fee table and TOTAL row state PHP 125.00 for new and updated renewal, and PHP 156.25 for late renewal. Payment is to the City Treasurer’s Office.

Application Form: Business Bureau Office, Window 1 or Public Assistance Desk. Certificate of Employment: applicant.

Checklist item 3 specifies Official Receipt (for service crew), from the City Treasurer’s Office. Separately, the process instructs walk-in applicants to submit required documents including the official receipt.

A notarized Affidavit of Consent is listed for minors below 18. For Night Clubs and related establishments and similar places of amusement, the affidavit is listed for ages 18 to 20.

Additional requirements for Entertainers, Masseurs, Bar Attendants: Birth Certificate (Philippine Statistics Authority); Valid ID of parent or qualified guardian for parent’s consent with appearance (Where to Secure: Any Notary public); Health ID (City Health).

The process note states: If the applicant is an entertainer, masseur, or bar attendant 18-20 years old, or the applicant is below 18 years old, he or she must present himself/herself for an interview. Agency action 2.2 repeats these conditions.

question: What is the procedure to permanently close a business in Davao City and what is the penalty for filing after 30 days?
reference_answer:
For Full Retirement of Business Permit after business operations cease, the charter gives these client steps (printed pages 112-114; PDF pages 73-75):

1. Submit requirements for pre-assessment, receive and sign the retirement application, then proceed to the City Treasurer’s Office for assessment of dues and approval for retirement.
2. Submit the recommended approved retirement application and Business Identification Plate and receive a claim stub.
3. Receive the retired business permit and the applicant’s copies of required documents; the processing staff receives the claim stub and releases them.

Checklist (printed page 111; PDF page 72). Each transcribed row includes Where to Secure; retain its ownership and representation conditions:

1. Latest Business Permit (1 original or 1 certified copy) Applicant or Records Section, Business Bureau
2. Affidavit of Full Retirement indicating the reason and the effective date of retirement if Single Proprietorship. (1 original) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
3. Partnership Resolution duly signed by all the Partners stating the reason, effective date of retirement and the authorized representative indicated therein if Partnership. (1 original) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
4. Board Resolution or Secretary’s Certificate stating the reason and effective date of retirement, the authorized represented indicated therein if other forms of ownership (1 original) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
5. Valid I.D. of the authorized representative, if newly designated (1 photocopy) Applicant
6. Special Power of Attorney for Single Proprietorship if represented (1 original) Any Notary Public / Applicant
7. Business Identification Plate Applicant

The TOTAL fee cell states Tax Obligation based on gross sales, and a late filing fee of P1,000 to P5,000 for an application filed more than 30 days from cessation. The cell does not specify how to choose an amount within that range.

question: Paano ang proseso ng full retirement ng business permit at magkano ang multa kung lumampas ng 30 days bago mag-file?
reference_answer:
For Full Retirement of Business Permit after business operations cease, the charter gives these client steps (printed pages 112-114; PDF pages 73-75):

1. Submit requirements for pre-assessment, receive and sign the retirement application, then proceed to the City Treasurer’s Office for assessment of dues and approval for retirement.
2. Submit the recommended approved retirement application and Business Identification Plate and receive a claim stub.
3. Receive the retired business permit and the applicant’s copies of required documents; the processing staff receives the claim stub and releases them.

Checklist (printed page 111; PDF page 72). Each transcribed row includes Where to Secure; retain its ownership and representation conditions:

1. Latest Business Permit (1 original or 1 certified copy) Applicant or Records Section, Business Bureau
2. Affidavit of Full Retirement indicating the reason and the effective date of retirement if Single Proprietorship. (1 original) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
3. Partnership Resolution duly signed by all the Partners stating the reason, effective date of retirement and the authorized representative indicated therein if Partnership. (1 original) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
4. Board Resolution or Secretary’s Certificate stating the reason and effective date of retirement, the authorized represented indicated therein if other forms of ownership (1 original) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
5. Valid I.D. of the authorized representative, if newly designated (1 photocopy) Applicant
6. Special Power of Attorney for Single Proprietorship if represented (1 original) Any Notary Public / Applicant
7. Business Identification Plate Applicant

The TOTAL fee cell states Tax Obligation based on gross sales, and a late filing fee of P1,000 to P5,000 for an application filed more than 30 days from cessation. The cell does not specify how to choose an amount within that range.

question: What are the physical facility requirements and fees to obtain ICAB accreditation for an internet cafe or pisonet business?
reference_answer: The ICAB checklist includes an ISP contract, certification or current receipt of payment; half-closed cubicles not more than 5 feet from the floor apply to Internet Cafes only. Lighting must be at least 25 Lux for fluorescent/LED lights or 50 Lux for incandescent lights. A warning sign at least 12 x 18 inches must state: no pornography, no gambling, no hacking, no minors prior to 6:00 AM and beyond 9:00 PM, and students may not play games during prescribed school hours. A system must block or filter pornographic sites/content; permanently fixed webcams are required for Internet Cafes only. The checklist also prohibits selling and consuming intoxicating drinks and cigarettes on the premises and lists a copy of ICAB ordinances 227-04, 0387-12 and 0270-15, as amended. Headphones, a urinal for 30 units and below, and separate male and female CRs for 31 units and above are listed for Internet Cafes only. For Internet Cafe and Pisonet owners, the fee cell states "PHP100.00 for the first 10 units and PHP10.00 for every unit". This wording is preserved without interpreting "every unit" as "each additional unit".

question: Unsa ang mga facility requirements ug pila ang bayad sa ICAB accreditation para sa pisonet o internet cafe?
reference_answer: The ICAB checklist includes an ISP contract, certification or current receipt of payment; half-closed cubicles not more than 5 feet from the floor apply to Internet Cafes only. Lighting must be at least 25 Lux for fluorescent/LED lights or 50 Lux for incandescent lights. A warning sign at least 12 x 18 inches must state: no pornography, no gambling, no hacking, no minors prior to 6:00 AM and beyond 9:00 PM, and students may not play games during prescribed school hours. A system must block or filter pornographic sites/content; permanently fixed webcams are required for Internet Cafes only. The checklist also prohibits selling and consuming intoxicating drinks and cigarettes on the premises and lists a copy of ICAB ordinances 227-04, 0387-12 and 0270-15, as amended. Headphones, a urinal for 30 units and below, and separate male and female CRs for 31 units and above are listed for Internet Cafes only. For Internet Cafe and Pisonet owners, the fee cell states "PHP100.00 for the first 10 units and PHP10.00 for every unit". This wording is preserved without interpreting "every unit" as "each additional unit".

question: How much is the Professional Tax Receipt (PTR) in Davao City and what are the requirements to secure it?
reference_answer:
The Professional Tax service lists a TOTAL fee of PHP300. Requirements: unexpired PRC/IBP ID (1 original); PRC/IBP certification for new registrants/passers (1 original); current Davao City address and valid contact number/email address.

Register/log in at ptr.davaocity.gov.ph, generate an Order of Payment, then pay at a Miscellaneous Fees counter or the listed Landbank payment portal.

question: What is the formula and statutory ceiling for computing individual and corporate Community Tax (Cedula) in Davao City?
reference_answer:
Annex14 states an annual basic community tax of PHP5 for liable individuals plus an annual additional tax of PHP1 per PHP1,000 of income, with the additional tax capped at PHP5,000. For husband and wife the additional tax is based on their total property and total gross receipts/earnings. The cap is on additional tax, not the basic-plus-additional total.

For liable corporations, the basic annual tax is PHP500 plus additional tax capped at PHP10,000. The additional schedule is PHP2 per PHP5,000 of Philippine real-property value during the preceding year using the stated real-property-tax valuation, plus PHP2 per PHP5,000 of Philippine business gross receipts/earnings during the preceding year. Intercorporate dividends are included in gross receipts/earnings for this additional tax. The cap is on additional tax.

question: What are the required documents to apply for an Occupancy Permit after completing building construction?
pillar: Office of the City Building Official
reference_answer:
Occupancy checklist: application letter (1 original); authorization letter if applicant is not owner (1 original); owner ID with 3 specimen signatures (1 photocopy); Certificate of Occupancy (1 original); Certificate of Completion (1 original); BFP Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (1 original); four-elevation project pictures (front/back/left/right); approved Building Construction, Architectural, Civil/Structural, Sanitary/Plumbing, Electrical and Mechanical installation permits (1 photocopy); approved building-permit plan (1 original).

If a different professional undertook/was assigned the project, the checklist requires a signed, notarized waiver from the previous professional in charge (1 original). It also lists Structure Images with CAAP clearance and structural survey for actual building height, signed/sealed by a licensed Geodetic Engineer. The authorization-letter source cell says CPDO and the picture source cell says Hired Geodetic Engineer; those unusual source associations are preserved.

question: What are the requirements and fee rates per linear meter to secure a Fencing Permit from OCBO?

reference_answer:
Fencing checklist: permit form with 3 sets of Civil/Architectural plans signed/sealed by licensed Civil Engineer/Architect (A3 structural-plan option stated); certified land title and property tax declaration (1 original and 1 photocopy each); the next row repeats Certified True Copy of Tax Declaration of the Property with CTO as source; Barangay Clearance (1 original and 1 photocopy); scaled sketch/lot/vicinity plan signed/sealed by licensed Geodetic Engineer (3 sets); bill of materials/cost estimates signed/sealed by licensed Civil Engineer (3 sets); signing professionals PRC ID/current PTR (1 photocopy); owner/applicant ID with 3 specimen signatures (1 photocopy); conditional DPWH clearance along a National Highway.

For fencing made of masonry, metal or concrete: height <= 1.80 m costs PHP3.00 per linear meter; height > 1.80 m costs PHP4.00 per linear meter. The service introduction says not exceeding 1.80 m, while the fee table explicitly includes a higher-height rate; this candidate reproduces the fee table without resolving that scope discrepancy.

question: Unsa ang mga papeles nga kailangan ug pila ang bayad kada linear meter para sa Fencing Permit kung magpader?
pillar: Office of the City Building Official
reference_answer:
Fencing checklist: permit form with 3 sets of Civil/Architectural plans signed/sealed by licensed Civil Engineer/Architect (A3 structural-plan option stated); certified land title and property tax declaration (1 original and 1 photocopy each); the next row repeats Certified True Copy of Tax Declaration of the Property with CTO as source; Barangay Clearance (1 original and 1 photocopy); scaled sketch/lot/vicinity plan signed/sealed by licensed Geodetic Engineer (3 sets); bill of materials/cost estimates signed/sealed by licensed Civil Engineer (3 sets); signing professionals PRC ID/current PTR (1 photocopy); owner/applicant ID with 3 specimen signatures (1 photocopy); conditional DPWH clearance along a National Highway.

For fencing made of masonry, metal or concrete: height <= 1.80 m costs PHP3.00 per linear meter; height > 1.80 m costs PHP4.00 per linear meter. Both printed source rows include "of fraction thereof". For indigenous materials, barbed, chicken or hog wire, the listed rate is PHP2.40 per linear meter. No additional height qualifier is stated in that row. The service introduction says not exceeding 1.80 m, while the fee table explicitly includes a higher-height rate; this candidate reproduces the fee table without resolving that scope discrepancy.

Para sa bayad, maaoy nga wala nay nakit-an sa mga nakapag-aral sa Citizens' Charter.

Para sa mga requirements, maaoy nga wala nay nakit-an sa [S2] ang nakit-an nga mga requirements para makakuha ug Certified True Copy sa nawala nga Building Permit. Ang mga nakit-an nga requirements sa [S2] ay:

1. Request Letter (Applicant)
2. Photocopy ng Building Permit at iba pang kasunduan (Applicant)
3. Photocopy ng Valid ID ng Owner (Applicant)

Sa [S3] ay wala nay nakit-an na nakit-an nga mga requirements para makakuha ug Certified True Copy sa nawala nga Building Permit. Ang [S3] ay tungkol sa Certifications o Certified True Copy na ibinibigay sa mga natural o juridical entity, government agencies o offices na gusto mag-aral sa kopya ng Business Permit o sa kahulugan ng status o record ng isang Taxpayer.

answer:
To obtain a CPDO Zoning Certification in Davao City, the following requirements are needed:

1. Submit original and photocopied O.R. with complete one (1) set of documents [S1, S2].
2. Obtain the borrow's consent [S2].
3. Certification that property is not within the Strategic Agriculture and Fisheries Development Zone (SAFDZ) from the Department of Agriculture [S2].
4. A visible project sign posted at the project site and a notice of pending application to be issued by the Zoning Administrator [S2].
5. A photo of the visible project sign [S2].
6. Notice of Pending Application published in a newspaper once a week for three (3) weeks [S2].

The processing fee for each hectare is PHP 750 [S3]. The total processing time is 3 days, 6 hours, and 50 minutes [S3].

question: What is the procedure, fee, and requirement checklist to appeal a denied Locational Clearance before the LZBAA?
reference_answer:
Motion for Reconsideration is an appeal against denial of Locational Clearance by the Zoning Administrator. The checklist lists: Letter of Reconsideration; Denial Letter; Order of Payment; Official Receipt; Business Permit Application Form/Building Permit Application Form (for building permit); certified true copy of title(s)/Contract of Lease/Deed of Sale; site sketch with vicinity map and landmarks; Barangay Council Resolution Interposing No Objection; affidavit of non-objection of adjoining property owners; locational mapping of neighbor consent signatories; Affidavit of Undertaking; and Building Permit for a business-permit application.

Secure checklist and pre-evaluation; once documents are complete, obtain the order for the PHP600 processing fee. Submit original and photocopied official receipt with one complete set of documents. The process includes TWG site inspection/evaluation, TWG meeting with the applicant, committee deliberation, and, if approved, resolution and endorsement to OBO or Business Bureau. Claim the endorsement with attached resolution. Non-approved/deferred cases may receive NOC, NOD or disapproval.

answer:
To appeal a denied Locational Clearance before the Local Zoning Board of Adjustments and Appeals (LZBAA), follow the procedure below:

1. Prepare a Letter of Reconsideration [S1, S3].
2. Obtain the Denial Letter from the City Planning and Development Office (CPDO) [S1, S3].
3. Submit the Letter of Reconsideration and Denial Letter to the Zoning Officer at the CPDO [S1].
4. The Zoning Officer will evaluate the application based on the proposed land use activity and its land classification [S2].
5. If the application is non-compliant, the client will receive a denial letter. Denied applications are advised to appeal through the LZBAA [S2].
6. If the application is conditionally approved, clients are required to submit additional requirements [S2].
7. The Zoning Officer will update the document tracking system for release [S3].
8. The Acting Administrative Officer at the CPDO will release the Denial Letter to the client [S3].
9. Denial Letters can be either delivered by the office or claimed at the office [S3].

There is no specified fee for appealing a denied Locational Clearance before the LZBAA in the provided sources.

question: Ano ang proseso, magkano ang processing fee, at ano ang kailangang ipasa kapag na-deny ang Locational Clearance at mag-aapela sa LZBAA?
reference_answer:
Motion for Reconsideration is an appeal against denial of Locational Clearance by the Zoning Administrator. The checklist lists: Letter of Reconsideration; Denial Letter; Order of Payment; Official Receipt; Business Permit Application Form/Building Permit Application Form (for building permit); certified true copy of title(s)/Contract of Lease/Deed of Sale; site sketch with vicinity map and landmarks; Barangay Council Resolution Interposing No Objection; affidavit of non-objection of adjoining property owners; locational mapping of neighbor consent signatories; Affidavit of Undertaking; and Building Permit for a business-permit application.

Secure checklist and pre-evaluation; once documents are complete, obtain the order for the PHP600 processing fee. Submit original and photocopied official receipt with one complete set of documents. The process includes TWG site inspection/evaluation, TWG meeting with the applicant, committee deliberation, and, if approved, resolution and endorsement to OBO or Business Bureau. Claim the endorsement with attached resolution. Non-approved/deferred cases may receive NOC, NOD or disapproval.

question: Under what structural conditions are FSCR, FSCCR, and FSMR required by the BFP, and who prepares them?
reference_answer: FSCR/FSCCR/FSMR are required if the building/facilities/structures are required to install any or a combination of wet standpipe, automatic fire suppression, or automatic fire detection and alarm systems. FSCR consists of plans, specifications and design analysis per building, prepared and duly signed by the Engineer/Architect-of-Record and his/her Fire Safety Practitioner. FSCCR compiles approved submittals, test and acceptance forms for fire protection and life safety features as part of as-built documents turned over by the contractor to the owner; it is duly signed by the Contractor/Construction Manager and his/her Fire Safety Practitioner. FSMR is prepared by the building owner, his/her fire safety practitioner or authorized representative, and duly signed by the Building Administrator and his/her Fire Safety Practitioner during regular annual fire safety inspection. The matrix associates FSCR with FSEC, FSCCR with occupancy FSIC, and FSMR with new business without valid occupancy-stage FSIC and the two renewal columns; blank cells are not exemption statements.
